weekend_note: Hurricane Isaias came ashore on the Panhandle Friday night, with more than 100,000 Escambia County customers without power by 8 PM, and recovery is expected to take longer than the storm itself. Saturday should be cooler and drier, with early temperatures in the low 60s and some lingering light showers, then sunshine Sunday with highs near 80. City event permits and rentals are canceled through Sunday, Pensacola Beach was under an evacuation order, and the Bay Center, UWF football and Blue Wahoos games are off. Treat any other weekend event as unconfirmed until the organizer says otherwise. The picks are next-week events and depend on storm recovery; only the Ice Flyers game on Oct 17 is indoors.

news.title: Isaias comes ashore on the Panhandle
news.summary: Live coverage from Bay News 9 says Isaias weakened to a Category 2 before landfall Friday night, with the eyewall moving onshore around 8 PM. More than 100,000 Escambia County customers had lost power by then, and flash flood warnings were extended in Fort Walton Beach. Final damage and rainfall totals were not yet reported.

news.title: Cooler, drier weather follows Isaias
news.summary: FOX10 expects Saturday to start in the low 60s with a few lingering light showers and breezy gusts, easing through the day. Sunday should be sunny with highs near 80. The station warns recovery may take longer than the storm and river flooding could develop after the rain ends.

news.title: City and county issue Friday evening storm update
news.summary: Evacuations covered Escambia Zones A and B. The Pensacola Bay, Theo Baars and Bob Sikes bridges were closed, as was Highway 399 on Santa Rosa Island. Pensacola's airport runways shut at 6 PM for damage checks with reopening not set, and the visitor centers aim to reopen Sunday if damage allows. The Perdido landfill and Palafox transfer station are slated to reopen Monday.

news.title: City asks residents to hold storm debris
news.summary: After the storm, the city says to wait for its debris collection plan and not to burn debris or pile it over storm drains, utility poles or in the roadway. Pickup may take days or weeks with several passes. Friday garbage and recycling collection moves to Monday, Oct 12.

news.title: Weekend events canceled or still on
news.summary: Fox Weather lists Festa Italiana as rebooked for November and the Gulf Shores shrimp festival as canceled, while the Pensacola Beach Songwriters Festival was said to be continuing through Sunday.

news.title: Games and shows called off
news.summary: The Southern Tip Off at the Bay Center, UWF's home football game and the Blue Wahoos' FSU-Auburn exhibition are canceled. The Saenger had listed its Thursday through Saturday shows as postponed.

coverage_note: Written around 3 AM Saturday Oct 10, just hours after Isaias made landfall, so conditions will change; confirm anything outdoors or on the beach with the organizer. Storm facts come from Bay News 9, FOX10, Fox Weather, WEAR and City of Pensacola notices. Many pages would not open this run (National Weather Service, Must Do Pensacola, Local Pulse, WUWF, CNN, NPR and NorthEscambia.com), so the highs, lows and rain chances for Oct 12 to 14 are carried over from earlier forecasts, Oct 10 and 11 use FOX10's description, and no forecast beyond Oct 14 was available. Event details are otherwise unchanged and no post-storm organizer updates were found; the Bay Center, UWF, Blue Wahoos and Festa Italiana changes remain confirmed. No damage reports for Pensacola proper had been published yet. North and west Escambia and Gonzalez coverage is thin and limited to county library classes already listed. Restaurant and business statuses are unchanged from last check; Pelican Bar and Grill and Casa Luvia remain unconfirmed.
